commitResults.messageBody:
JavaDoc tags and method headers use inconsistent formatting, which makes the public API documentation harder to scan.

Standardize tags, convert short headers to multi-line Javadocs, use American spelling, and wrap the overlong error message.

Java code changes need a consistent project-specific standard to follow.

Add the SE-EDU Java coding-standard skill and require agents to load it
before Java code work.

Future commits need a shared convention for messages and branch names.

Add the SE-EDU Git-standard skill and require agents to load it before
proposing or creating commits.

Configure Gradle to run Checkstyle 11.0.0 against production and test sources.\n\nAdd rules based on the SE-EDU Java coding standard and suppressions for test Javadocs that are intentionally optional.

Configure Gradle with the JavaFX dependencies required by the tutorial.

Add the JavaFX Application and separate launcher classes so the project
can start the HelloWorld stage through ./gradlew run.

commitResults.messageTitle: Bundle JavaFX for the build machine's architecture
commitResults.messageBody:
The bundled JAR contains Intel macOS libraries even when Gradle runs on
Apple Silicon. Launching it with a Java 25 runtime without JavaFX fails
because those libraries cannot load on ARM64.

Select the macOS JavaFX dependencies for the architecture of the Java
runtime running Gradle. Retain the Windows and Linux dependencies.

Bundle only one macOS architecture per JAR because the native library
filenames are shared between the Intel and Apple Silicon variants.
This lets the Apple Silicon build run without a separate JavaFX install.

Validation: rebuild the bundled JAR and confirm that it launches and
renders with a Java 25 runtime that contains no JavaFX modules.

The README explains IDE setup but does not explain how to package or
run the application with its JavaFX dependencies included.

Without packaging guidance, users can distribute the ordinary JAR and
encounter missing JavaFX dependencies on another computer.

Document the Shadow JAR build command, output path, Java 25 requirement,
launch command, and expected Hello World window. Explain the native
library coverage and the need to match the macOS build architecture.

Keep these instructions in the README so the build and distribution
workflow is available alongside the existing setup instructions.

Validation: check the commands and output against the successful JAR
build and launch using a Java 25 runtime without JavaFX modules.

commitResults.messageTitle: Assert validated task data during development
commitResults.messageBody:
Task constructors rely on the command parser to supply descriptions,
deadline dates, and event times that have already been validated.
Violating these assumptions can leave invalid state inside a task.

Document those internal contracts with Java assert statements and
diagnostic messages. Enable assertions for Gradle runs and tests, and
document the -ea flag for direct JAR launches.

Keep user-input validation in the command parser so ordinary input
errors still receive helpful messages even when assertions are disabled.
Add tests that verify assertion failures for invalid internal task data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Separate task parsing from application flow
commitResults.messageBody:
Arin's main class coordinates commands and also contains all task
parsing rules. Long parsing branches and numeric separator offsets make
those rules harder to review and test independently. The UI also repeats
the numbered-list layout for ordinary lists and search results.

Extract task creation into TaskParser with a focused method per task
type and named separators. Delegate both list views to a shared display
helper, preserving their headings, numbering, and task order.

Keep command syntax, error messages, and storage representations intact
so the refactor improves readability without changing user behavior.
Add parser regression tests and retain the exact-output UI tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use streams for task search and storage conversion
commitResults.messageBody:
Task searching and storage conversion each build a result list with an
explicit loop. Their intent is to filter matching tasks or map tasks to
storage lines, which Java streams can express directly.

Use a filter pipeline for case-insensitive search and a map pipeline
for task serialization. Preserve encounter order, duplicate entries,
and the existing storage format.

Collect search results into a separate mutable ArrayList to preserve
the previous behavior. Keep Locale.ROOT normalization so matching does
not depend on the computer's default locale.

Add regression tests for empty inputs, duplicates, result-list mutation,
locale-independent matching, and ordered storage output.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match task assertions to parser whitespace rules
commitResults.messageBody:
Task parsing validates details with trim(), whereas isBlank() recognizes
additional Unicode whitespace. An assertion using isBlank() can reject
input that the parser accepts, turning a user command into an internal
assertion failure when development checks are enabled.

Use the same trim-based emptiness rule in task assertions as in the
parser. Add a Unicode em-space regression test to keep assertion-enabled
execution consistent with ordinary command validation.

Task constructors rely on validated descriptions, dates, and event times.

Integrate Java assertions for these internal contracts and enable them
for development runs and tests. Preserve ordinary validation behavior,
including the parser's existing Unicode whitespace rules.

Validation: all 23 tests and both Checkstyle tasks pass with Java 25.
Malformed CLI commands still produce user-facing error messages.

commitResults.messageTitle: Sync A-Streams with the code quality refactor
commitResults.messageBody:
Master now includes the extracted task parser and shared list renderer.
The streams branch must include that latest base before its final merge.

Merge master into A-Streams and preserve the search and serialization

Task search and storage conversion use explicit collection loops.

Integrate stream filtering and mapping while preserving task order,
duplicates, locale-independent matching, mutable search results, and
the existing storage format. Sync with both earlier increments before
merging so assertions, parsing, and streams are verified together.

Validation: all 47 JUnit tests, both Checkstyle tasks, the standalone
exit test, and the bundled JAR build and CLI smoke test pass on Java 25.
